chunks: He said: Abul Mudhaffar Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Balkhi reported to me, he said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abul-Thalj narrated to us, he said: Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Hasani narrated to us, he said: Isa ibn Mihran narrated to us, he said: Hafs ibn Umar al-Farra narrated to us, he said: Abu Muadh al-Khazzaz narrated to us, he said: Yunus ibn Abd al-Warith narrated to me from his father, who said:

Once Ibn Abbas was addressing us from the pulpit at Basrah. When he turned his face towards the people and said: "O group of people, bewildered in their religious affairs! By God, if you had given precedence to he who Allah had given precedence, and put back he who Allah had put back, and if you had kept the heritage and the authority where Allah had kept them, no part of divine determinate share would have been unfairly distributed, and no friend of Allah would have been humiliated, and no two persons would have differed on the law of Allah. So taste the evil consequence of your negligence about what you sent forth,"
"and those who do wrong shall come to know what punishment awaits them."

key_terms.الوراثة: Inheritance/heritage — refers to the divinely-designated prophetic succession
key_terms.الولاية: Wilayah (authority/guardianship) — the legitimate authority given by God to the Ahlulbayt
key_terms.عال: To be unfairly distributed or transgressed — used here for the shares of divine law

ai.seo_question: What did Ibn Abbas say about the succession of the Prophet and the authority of Ahlulbayt?
ai.summary: Abdullah ibn Abbas, the Prophet's cousin who served as governor of Basrah, delivered this sermon to the people of Basrah rebuking them for abandoning the divinely-appointed succession and authority (wilayah). He argued that all the community's religious disagreements and injustices stem from ignoring God's designation of leadership, and concluded with the Quranic warning from Surah al-Shu'ara (26:227) about the fate of the wrongdoers.
word_analysis: and they shall come to know
